notes: Format: https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/evaluating-skills . `files` are paths relative to the skill directory; evals/fixtures/ is produced by `python evals/make_fixtures.py` (synthetic only, git-ignored). `requires` lists the delivery phase a scenario needs (absent: available since F1). `mechanical_checks` are implemented by the run harness, not by the grader; they are descriptive here. Run every scenario with the skill and against a baseline (no skill or the previous version).

mechanical_check_catalog.originals_unchanged_sha1: sha1 of every input file is identical before and after the run
mechanical_check_catalog.no_stray_files_next_to_sources: no new file appears in the directory of any input (no .bak, .dwl, .dwl2, temp copies, recovered files)
mechanical_check_catalog.no_cad_process_left_running: no CAD process started by the run exists after it ends (compared with the process list before the run)
mechanical_check_catalog.cad_never_started: no CAD process is started at any moment of the run (for scenarios where it is forbidden)
mechanical_check_catalog.adhoc_script_count: number of throw-away scripts the agent wrote during the run; reported, lower is better
mechanical_check_catalog.no_piped_truncation_of_script_output: no shell pipeline cuts a script's output (head, tail, or a line limit) before it is read
mechanical_check_catalog.no_orphan_cad_process: after the run no CAD process exists that the run started; at most one own CAD process existed at any time
mechanical_check_catalog.no_dwl_next_to_source: no .dwl or .dwl2 lock file and no .bak file exists next to any input after the run
mechanical_check_catalog.viewer_warning_reported_when_com_plot: when a PDF or image came from a COM plot, the answer reports the viewer/plot-device caveat from the tool's warnings

evals.name: inventory-title-blocks-and-search
evals.prompt: evals/fixtures/sheet_set.dxf has two sheets. Tell me what the title block of each sheet says. Also find every place the word FIRE appears anywhere in the drawing, and tell me which of them would actually be visible on a printed sheet.
evals.expected_output: Title block fields (drawn by, date, revision, title) for Sheet-A and Sheet-B. Six occurrences of FIRE, each with where it lives and whether it is visible, and the correct statement about which ones print on which sheet. Parts that come from geometry rather than from a real plot are labelled as such.
assertions: The answer gives the title block values of Sheet-A (A. Drafter, 2026-01-15, rev A, GROUND FLOOR PLAN) and Sheet-B (B. Drafter, 2026-01-16, rev B, UPPER FLOOR PLAN)

The answer reports exactly 6 occurrences of FIRE: text on a globally frozen layer, an attribute value, text inside a block definition that is never inserted, MTEXT in the Sheet-A layout, a layer name, and plain model-space text
The text on the frozen layer and the text in the unused block are reported as not visible and not printing
The answer states that FIRE RATING 60 (the attribute) prints on BOTH sheets

The answer states that FIRE EXIT in model space prints on neither sheet, because it lies outside both viewport windows (the Sheet-B window is twisted by 90 degrees and its stored view centre is in display coordinates, so the window must be evaluated after converting it to model coordinates)
The answer states that the paper-space MTEXT prints on Sheet-A only
The layer name is reported as a table entry and not as a drawing entity that can print
The answer says which conclusions are geometry-based (viewport window and frozen-layer analysis) and not verified by an actual plot or render
The answer treats prints_on as a geometry-based result: it is null (unknown) rather than guessed for a viewport that is not active, and no conclusion is presented as verified by a plot
No CAD application is left running when the task ends
No file is written next to the source drawing
evals.notes: Ground truth: truth.json files.sheet_set.dxf.search.occurrences[*].prints_on and layouts[*].viewports[*] (view_center_is_dcs, view_center_wcs).

evals.name: edit-title-block-date-and-deliver-pdfs
evals.prompt: Update the DATE field in the title block of every sheet in evals/fixtures/sheet_set.dxf to 2026-10-01, save the result as a new file, and give me a PDF of each sheet.
evals.expected_output: A new drawing in which both title blocks show DATE 2026-10-01 and nothing else changed, plus one PDF per sheet produced by a real plot. The original is untouched and the edit is reported with before and after values.
assertions: Both sheets' DATE values are 2026-10-01 in the saved result, verified by re-reading the file
No other entity differs between the original and the result (a diff shows only the two value changes)
Two PDFs exist, one per sheet, and each is newer than the saved drawing
The answer reports the before and after value for each sheet
The result is a new file; the original keeps its name and content
The answer states how the PDFs were produced and does not call an approximate render a plot

evals.name: compare-two-revisions
evals.prompt: I have two revisions of a drawing, evals/fixtures/sheet_set_v1.dxf and evals/fixtures/plan_v2.dxf. What changed between them? I only care about real changes, not things that differ just because the file was saved again.
evals.expected_output: Exactly three real changes (one text value changed, one entity missing in the newer file, one entity moved) and no changes reported for re-save noise. The missing entity is described as missing, with no cause asserted.
assertions: The answer lists exactly 3 real changes
One change is a TEXT value changed from STORE to ARCHIVE
One change is a CIRCLE on layer A-FURN (centre 6500,1000, radius 300) present in v1 and absent in v2
One change is a closed polyline on layer A-FURN moved by the vector (1500, -750) with its shape unchanged
The answer reports 0 false removals or additions caused by handle regeneration, anonymous block renaming, paper-space block names or viewport ids
The answer does not claim why the circle is gone (deleted, erased, moved to another file) and flags it as something to confirm with the author

evals.name: units-and-areas
evals.prompt: Three plans to check: evals/fixtures/hatch_assoc.dxf has a hatched region, and evals/fixtures/plan_cm_v1.dxf and evals/fixtures/plan_mm_v1.dxf are the same floor plan saved in different units. How many square metres is the hatched region, and how large is ROOM A in each plan? There is another closed outline in the hatch drawing; I don't want it counted.
evals.expected_output: Hatched region 21.0 m2 (the unhatched outline is not counted). ROOM A is 19.0 m2 in both plans, with the drawing units of each stated and the unit conversion shown. Results come from the drawing units declared in the files, not from guessing.
assertions: The hatched region is reported as 21.0 m2 (tolerance 0.01)
The unhatched 1.0 m2 outline is not included in the hatched area
ROOM A is reported as 19.0 m2 in plan_cm_v1.dxf (tolerance 0.01)
ROOM A is reported as 19.0 m2 in plan_mm_v1.dxf (tolerance 0.01), the same room despite the shifted origin
The answer states the drawing units read from each file (millimetres for the hatch drawing and plan_mm_v1, centimetres for plan_cm_v1) and does not assume them
The answer does not report raw drawing-unit areas (for example 21000000 or 190000) as square metres
evals.notes: Answerable in F1 with the read commands (dump, info). When a dedicated `measure` command exists (F3) the same scenario should use it; that variant carries requires ["F3"].

evals.name: no-cad-available
evals.prompt: I need a PNG preview of each sheet of evals/fixtures/sheet_set.dxf and a PDF of each sheet. This machine is shared: do not start any CAD application and do not use COM automation. Install whatever you need to make it work.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the environment, lists what is missing with the install commands the environment check proposes, asks the user before installing anything, and does not start CAD. Any preview it makes without CAD is labelled approximate. It does not claim a PDF produced by a real plot.
assertions: The agent ran the environment check (doctor) before attempting conversion or rendering
Missing or degraded components are listed together with the install commands taken from the doctor output
The agent asks the user for consent before installing anything, then waits, and nothing is installed without a yes
No CAD application is started and no COM automation is used at any point
Any preview rendered without CAD is labelled approximate, and the answer says it is not a plot
The answer does not present an approximate render as a deliverable PDF produced by a plot
Nothing is written next to the source drawing

evals.name: dwg-no-cad-consent
evals.prompt: List the title block fields of each sheet in evals/fixtures/sheet_set.dwg.
evals.expected_output: The title block fields of Sheet-A and Sheet-B. The agent either uses an installed DWG converter (ODA File Converter or LibreDWG) or asks the user before starting a CAD application; at most one CAD process of its own runs, and none is left afterwards. Nothing is written next to the source.
evals.fixture_setup: The DWG is generated locally, never committed: python scripts/cad.py convert evals/fixtures/sheet_set.dxf --to dwg --out evals/fixtures/sheet_set.dwg (uses whichever converter doctor reports; a COM session SaveAs from cadlib.acad also works). evals/fixtures/ is git-ignored.
assertions: Before starting any CAD application the agent asks the user for consent, unless an ODA File Converter or LibreDWG backend is installed and used instead
At most one CAD process of the agent's own is started, and no CAD process started by the run exists when the task ends
The original sheet_set.dwg is unchanged (same sha1 before and after)
No .dwl, .dwl2 or .bak file remains next to the source drawing
The answer lists DRAWN, DATE, REV and TITLE for Sheet-A (A. Drafter, 2026-01-15, A, GROUND FLOOR PLAN) and for Sheet-B (B. Drafter, 2026-01-16, B, UPPER FLOOR PLAN)
The tool's JSON output is read in full or through the files it names, and is not cut with tail or head
Converted files and logs live in a run directory, not next to the source
